did_you_know.text: Did you know? After David finished speaking with Saul, Jonathan became deeply attached to him and loved him as himself.
Did you know? Jonathan gave David his robe, his armor, his sword, his bow, and his belt—an expression of the covenant of love they made.
Did you know? Saul appointed David over the men of war after David succeeded in every mission he was sent on, and David pleased both the people and Saul’s officers.

Did you know? The women’s song after David returned from battle compared Saul’s achievements—saying he had struck down thousands—with David’s achievements, saying he had struck down tens of thousands.
Did you know? The women’s song aroused Saul’s jealousy, and he feared that David would also receive the kingdom after being praised more highly than Saul.
Did you know? Saul tried to strike David with a spear and pin him to the wall, but David managed to escape him twice.
Did you know? Although Saul was afraid of David, all Israel and Judah loved him because he went out and came in before them—in other words, he led them in their activities and battles.
Did you know? Saul had promised David his older daughter, Merab, but when the time came for the marriage, she was given to Adriel the Meholathite.
Did you know? Saul demanded one hundred Philistine foreskins from David as a condition for marrying Michal, but David and his men brought the king two hundred.
Did you know? Whenever the Philistine commanders went out to battle, David was more successful than all of Saul’s officers, so his name became widely known and highly honored.
